source.title: Glassy dynamics near the interpolation transition in deep recurrent networks.

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates test loss across widths near the interpolation transition and over training time, using deep recurrent networks on Bach chorales. This is a different setting and measurement from the original studies, and its test-loss results bear directly on V1 and V2.
record.gate_note: Appendix D reports test-loss curves for a two-hidden-layer network at widths 35, 70, and 140. The authors state that these results do not show a test-loss maximum around the interpolation transition, and that test losses reach an early minimum and then rise smoothly. Training-loss and weight-fluctuation results do not measure the claim's test-error behavior; cited findings from other studies are not included.
record.test_reason: The paper is mainly about the training dynamics of deep recurrent networks on Bach chorales: critical slowing down and aging. Only Appendix D bears on the claim. It tracks test loss over 1.5M steps for depth-2 networks at widths 35, 70 and 140, near half, at and twice the critical width. The authors state there is no test-loss maximum around the interpolation transition. That is a result on V1 and V2 in a new setting (recurrent nets, music data), so T3 rather than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase covers only Appendix D, and is accurate for it: no test-loss peak was seen, possibly because of the small training set, and much longer runs might change the width-70 vs width-140 ordering. The paper's main conclusions are different. Training approaches the interpolation transition with critical slowing down (learning time ∝ 1/(w−wc)), and the loss decays as a power law. Underparametrized networks show spin-glass-like aging, which in overparametrized networks persists until learning is nearly finished. Recurrence does not qualitatively change these dynamics.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies recurrent networks trained on Bach chorales and reports a limited test-loss width sweep and training trajectories; it does not present these as a reproduction of the original double-descent experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The test-loss evidence is limited to depth 2 and widths 35, 70, and 140. The authors note that training-set size and possibly a much longer training duration could affect whether a peak appears.

fits_no_version.finding: Learning time to reach small training loss diverges roughly as 1/(w−wc) approaching the interpolation transition from the overparametrized side. Aging-like weight fluctuations appear in the underparametrized phase.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training dynamics show critical slowing down and glassy aging near the interpolation threshold (training loss, not test error).

record.problems: The test-loss study is limited to three widths and a 1.5-million-step run; numerical values are only in a figure. The authors identify the small training set as a possible explanation and say an order-of-magnitude longer run might change the relative curves. The paper also reports that its long learning runs generally relied on single runs and single weight initializations.
record.rows_left_out: No further test-loss outcomes reported separately in text were identified. Training-loss, critical-slowing, and aging measurements were left out because they do not measure test error; cited results from other studies were also excluded.

untested.parts: Only three widths at depth 2; no label noise; no other depths, architectures or datasets; dense width sweep absent.
Behaviour beyond 1.5M steps; settings with label noise; other depths and architectures.
No label-noise or regularization manipulation; no multiple peaks examined.
No re-plotting of test loss against an effective parameter count. Fig. 7b uses parameter count only for training-loss thresholds.

record.verdict_notes: The double-descent evidence is a minor appendix result: figure-only, three widths, single runs, and a training set that may differ from the main one (the appendix says it reused the Fig. 6 data; Fig. 6 is captioned 80 chorales, the text says 100). No label noise was used, and the original sources found model-wise and epoch-wise peaks weakest without noise. Both challenges labels should therefore be read as holding for this small, noise-free recurrent setting only.

versions.untested_parts: Other architectures, datasets, depths, and size ranges beyond the reported two-hidden-layer recurrent networks at widths 35, 70, and 140.
Other architectures and training runs beyond the reported test-loss trajectories; whether substantially longer runs would show a later second descent.
No training-sample-size sweep near the interpolation threshold.
No comparison across model classes testing whether capacity growth past interpolation yields a second descent.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location across size, epochs, and sample count.
No test of label-noise or regularization dependence, multiple peaks, or disappearance under optimally tuned regularization.
No comparison of the curve under an alternative effective-parameter count.
